_about: The reference data every new unit starts with: project types, rules of credit, the scorecard, the glossary and the non-project charge codes. A unit's own copy can be edited on Reference.

project_types.name: Detailed Design
project_types.notes: Baseline type. Full production of drawings, models and calculations.

project_types.name: Concept / Preliminary Design
project_types.notes: High engineering content, low document count. Weighted above DD for option-development effort.

project_types.name: Feasibility / Master Planning
project_types.notes: Study work ending in a report rather than a drawing set.

project_types.name: Specialist Analysis & Modelling
project_types.notes: Numerical analysis and modelling delivered in its own right: structural and seismic, hydraulic and flood, traffic, energy and daylight, geotechnical, mooring and wave. Highest weight - specialist, non-substitutable skill.

project_types.name: Design Review / Third-Party Check
project_types.notes: Checking another party's design. Real skill, but consumes rather than creates deliverables.

project_types.name: Tender Documentation
project_types.notes: BOQ, specifications and tender drawings assembled from completed design.

project_types.name: Construction Phase Support
project_types.notes: Reactive scope. Measured on closed queries, not on time at desk.

project_types.name: Proposals & Bids
project_types.notes: Necessary but unmeasurable against a budget. Excluded from CPI by design.

project_types.name: On Hold / Standby
project_types.notes: Dormant scope. Earns no value; time booked here should be minimal and visible.

scorecard_factors.how: Best performer scores 100; others in proportion. Earned MM is weighted by project type factor — scoring only.
100 when exactly on target; falls away as it deviates either side.
100 when exactly on plan; over- and under-running both lose points.
Rewards absolute value delivered, weighted by project type factor — scoring only.

definitions.means: The effort we SAID we would spend in this period. It comes from each project's budget spread across the months between its start and end date, so a 12 MM project running 2 years contributes 1.5 MM to each quarter.
definitions.how: Straight-line spread of Budget across the project's start-to-end window, summed for every project touching the period.

definitions.means: The effort we REALLY spent in this period — the man-months your team actually booked against projects in those three months (or that year).
definitions.how: The hours booked to projects in the quarters inside the selected period, across all projects and everyone on the team, in man-months.

definitions.means: The VALUE we delivered in this period, expressed in man-months of budget. If a project is 70% complete on a 26 MM budget, 18.2 MM of value has been earned regardless of how long it took.
definitions.how: Budget x % Complete for each project, then spread across quarters in proportion to when the time was actually booked.

definitions.means: Value delivered less effort burned, in this period only. Positive means you got more budget-value out than man-months you put in.
How much the team could deliver in this period if fully applied to projects.
definitions.how: Each person's availability % for that year x 3 months per quarter (x4 for a full year), summed across the team.

definitions.means: How busy the team was: how much of the available capacity was actually booked to projects.
definitions.how: Actual MM divided by Capacity MM.

definitions.means: Did we burn the effort we said we would this period?
definitions.how: Actual MM divided by Planned MM.

definitions.means: Value delivered per man-month spent, IN THIS PERIOD ONLY. Above 1.00 means the period converted effort into progress well.
definitions.how: Earned MM in period divided by Actual MM in period.

definitions.means: No time was booked to any project in the period, so there is nothing to divide.
A project is marked well advanced on very little booked time, so earned value dwarfs actual effort.
More effort has been spent than value delivered. This is a genuine overrun.
Period figures are volatile by nature — one quarter of light logging moves them a long way.

non_project_codes.meaning: Personal excuse, part of a day
Late arrival, part of a day
